fact: The Ministry reports that in 2021, with GIZ, it rolled out the dLRev revenue software in 114 of Ghana's 260 MMDAs (43.8%, Ministry's own count); this is a roll-out, with no figure for assemblies actually recording in it.
E-billing and e-payment modules were added to dLRev in the 114 MMDAs; the document does not say whether a register of payers is held, so it is read as receipts.

The Ministry of Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development rolled dLRev out in collaboration with GIZ and plans in 2022 to build on dLRev and other applications to administer revenue in all MMDAs.
The document names GIZ as collaborator on the dLRev roll-out but gives no budget line or donor funding for it.
In 2021 dLRev reached 114 MMDAs and e-billing and e-payment modules were introduced.

dLRev holds a fiscal cadastre of businesses and properties (owner, type, location) linked to a digital address map, and manages billing and collection of property rates and business operating permits; the paper's 2019 data covers nine assemblies using it.
From 2017 dLRev has been hosted on the National IT Agency (NITA) national platform, so districts are set up remotely and there are no standalone operations.
Nine of Ghana's 260 MMDAs (3.5%) used dLRev throughout 2019 to collect property and business rates, per the GIZ-commissioned paper.
Fifty-two of 260 MMDAs (20.0%) were set up on the dLRev platform by the end of 2019, per the paper; 38 more were at SNPA and data-collection stages.

In February 2020 dLRev showed 47 of the 90 GIZ partner districts with properties registered for rates and 45 with businesses registered for operating permits; 60 had spatial data and 49 had fee-fixing loaded; no national total is given.
A 2017 survey by Dzansi et al. cited in the paper found 17.8% of the 260 MMDAs used software to send bills or demand notices and 33% had an electronic database for businesses or properties.
Dutch VNG International piloted a different revenue collection system, Taxman, in parts of three assemblies (KEEA, Cape Coast, Shama) alongside dLRev in 2019-2020.
Before dLRev most assemblies issued hand-written bills and demand notices; seven of the eight assemblies profiled in the 2016 SfDR baseline billed by hand.
dLRev was developed and implemented by GIZ with the Ministry (MLGRD); the paper says the software will be licensed and handed over to the Ministry in 2020.
The application was funded by GIZ, with USAID, Global Affairs Canada and Switzerland funding support to additional districts.
The paper names no national costed plan for dLRev scale-up and notes concern about sustainability after handover; the 2020 National Budget is cited as stating 83 MMDAs will introduce dLRev.

In 2019 the Revenue Collection App (offline-capable, on-the-spot collection) became ready for use, with payer, defaulter and payment registers, and 2020 SMS billing and GhIPSS mobile-payment modules were added.
